# Summary of Cairn System Rules

## Rule C1: The Pulse
A pulse makes a cairn taller by adding: the stride value plus a count of complete stride-sized chunks already in the cairn. Taller cairns grow more because they contain more complete strides.

## Rule C2: Repeated Pulses
When pulsing multiple times, you must recalculate the stride count fresh after each pulse. The number of complete strides changes as the cairn grows, so each successive pulse adds a different amount than the previous one.

## Rule C3: The Leak
A leak removes marks after a pulse occurs (not before). The amount lost equals one mark per complete leak-sized group in the new height. So you pulse first, then calculate and remove the leak based on that taller height.

## Rule C4: Finding the Origin
You can work backwards from a final height to discover the starting height by reversing pulses one at a time. Since pulses always increase height in a consistent way, there's only one possible starting height that leads to any given final height.

## Rule C5: Draining
Draining involves repeated cycles of pulse-then-remove. The cairn empties only if the drain amount exceeds what each pulse adds. You cannot simply divide the starting height by the drain to find how many cycles occur—the actual number is larger because pulse amounts vary as height changes.

## Rule C6: Merging
Two cairns combine using proportional shares (expressed in tenths) that determine what fraction of each contributes. You multiply each share by its cairn's height, round down, then add a tether bonus. The formula is: floor(w × q₁) + floor((1-w) × q₂) + b
